title.narrative: Re-enforcing Primary Healthcare and Mobile Health Services with Integrated Malaria and Nutrition Interventions in Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aligns with the 2025 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and the NHF Second Standard Allocation strategy, prioritizing lifesaving community centered interventions to reduce morbidity and mortality, protect livelihoods with an integrated package of services that include provision of essential health services to reduce preventable deaths, nutritional support to prevent and treat acute malnutrition, safe water and sanitation to curb disease outbreaks and protection services to safeguard at-risk groups, while enhancing local capacities to ensure timely, context-specific responses. This will be achieved through the delivery of an integrated, community-centered health response to address the urgent needs of vulnerable populations in Borno State, during the 2025 lean season. The project will target 50,000 populations in Bulabulin Ngarnam Communities in Bolori 2 Ward of Maiduguri with interventions to strengthen access to lifesaving services through health facility and community-based approaches as follows:ltbrgt1. Support one Primary Healthcare Centre (Bulabulin-Ngarnam PHC) and expand mobile clinic (MC) to reach undeserved areas. This will ensure the provision of essential health services including treatment of common illnesses, malnutrition, immunizations, deliveries, antenatal and post-natal care, provision of Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEMONC), Gender Based Violence Prevention and Response, mental health and psycho-social support Services (MHPSS), and referral services in hard-to-reach areas. ltbrgt2. To strengthen disease surveillance and outbreak response, the project will train and deploy Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) in collaboration with the State Ministry of Health to strengthen early detection, reporting, and containment of disease outbreaks such as malaria, cholera, and measles. ltbrgt3. Malaria prevention will be a key focus, with the implementation of targeted vector control activities in high-risk communities complemented by community-based awareness sessions ( IEC/BCC) to promote hygiene practices, malaria prevention, and health-seeking behaviours. MENTOR will implement lifesaving integrated vector management to reduce cases and prevent outbreaks of malaria and other VBDs through the distribution of WHO approved Spatial Repellents targeting IDPs and host populations in communities having high levels of malaria/VBD burden. ltbrgt4. The project will also address malnutrition through community screening of children under five (CU5) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), with referrals to Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFPs) as needed. Integrated maternal and child health and nutrition counselling will be provided at PHCs and during MC visits to promote optimal feeding practices and improve nutritional outcomes.ltbrgt5. Community engagement is central to the project’s design and implementation. Local leaders, women and youth groups will be involved in planning and delivery of health messages, facilitate referrals, and support feedback mechanisms, while ensuring that activities are culturally appropriate, inclusive, and responsive to the needs and priorities of affected populations. ltbrgt6. To support maternal and newborn health and promote safe hygiene practices, MENTOR will distribute hygiene and delivery kits at supported PHC with priority given to malnourished PLW and caregivers of malnourished CU5.ltbrgt7. Activities will be implemented with a strong focus on cross-cutting themes, including Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), gender equality, and disability inclusion.ltbrgtBy integrating facility-based services with mobile outreach and community engagement, the project will contribute to the NHF 2025 strategic objective of reducing excess mortality and morbidity, while strengthening local health systems and community resilience in Borno State.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
